fields.fieldText: DELAYS IN SENDING FAXES In order to identify if there are delays when sending faxes, the Fax Log tool in the Admin Interface will need to be used to diagnose the problems. USING THE FAX LOG TOOL TO GATHER INFORMATION OF THE FAILED OUTBOUND FAXES Ask the customer of the phone number(s) they had problems sending faxes to, as well as the dates of when they encountered the issues. Using the Fax Log tool, narrow down the results by filtering the date range of when the customer experienced the issues. Click View once the dates are set. Once the results are loaded, it will show up a list of all faxes that were processed by RingCentral in the account within the specific date range. The image above shows a 1-page fax request sent by albee.delacruz@ringcentral.com on 06/22/2017 at 5:58:31 PM. NOTE: An Email-to-Fax transaction processed by RingCentral will be indicated by a Message ID and Submit Date (date/time when RingCentral received the email) along with the trusted email address attempting to send a fax under the From Number. The results shown here does not automatically indicate that the fax was successfully sent by RingCentral. Click the Message ID to view the details of the fax transaction. The image above shows that the 1-page fax request sent by albee.delacruz@ringcentral.com was successfully sent to phone number: 1 (650) 539-3557 on 6/22/2017 at 5:59:42 PM.

screens.name: DETERMINE_IF_THE_EMAIL_ADDRESS_IS_AUTHORIZED_TO_USE_THE_EMAIL_TO_FAX_SERVICE
screens.label: DETERMINE IF THE EMAIL ADDRESS IS AUTHORIZED TO USE THE EMAIL-TO-FAX SERVICE

fields.name: tile7a
fields.fieldText:
DETERMINE IF THE EMAIL ADDRESS IS AUTHORIZED TO USE THE EMAIL-TO-FAX SERVICE When a user sends a fax via email, RingCentral checks the email address of the sender and only sends the fax if it follows all conditions below:
  • The email address the fax will be sent from is added to the User Extension's Trusted Email Addresses list. If the email address is not in the Trusted Email Addresses list, it should be the contact email of the User Extension.
  • The email address must not be added to multiple Accounts or User Extensions' Trusted Email Addresses list, nor be the contact email of multiple User Extensions.
    • To easily check if this is the case, using the Admin Tool, lookup the email address being used by the customer and determine if multiple records will show up.

screens.name: DETERMINE_IF_THE_EMAIL_RECEIVED_FROM_THE_CUSTOMER_CONTAINS_ANY_SUBJECT
screens.label: DETERMINE IF THE EMAIL RECEIVED FROM THE CUSTOMER CONTAINS ANY SUBJECT

fields.name: tile3ac
fields.fieldText:
DETERMINE IF THE EMAIL RECEIVED FROM THE CUSTOMER CONTAINS ANY SUBJECT Even if the customer leaves the subject line blank when sending an Email-to-Fax, some email services replaces a blank subject line with automated text such as:
  • NO SUBJECT
  • (No Subject)
  • "No Subject"
  • < >
This causes the RingCentral processing server to think that the sender included a text in the subject line hence a cover page will still be sent. Analyze the email received from the customer and determine if the subject line is empty.

screens.label: DETERMINING THE PROBLEM BASED ON THE FAX LOG RESULTS

fields.name: tile3delays
fields.fieldText:
DETERMINING THE PROBLEM BASED ON THE FAX LOG RESULTS Below are the different statuses that customers may encounter when sending faxes using email: FAILED - RENDERING FAILED
  • This generally indicates that the RingCentral processing server could not read the attachment.
FAILED
  • This indicates that RingCentral has processed the sending of the fax however it encountered an error connecting to the destination fax machine.
SENT
  • This indicates that RingCentral has processed the sending of the fax and successfully connected to the destination fax machine.
NOT RENDERED / MARKED
  • This indicates that the RingCentral processing server has just received the request to send the fax and is currently analyzing the document and/or cover page attached to the email.
  • This may also indicate that the request to send the fax is currently queued.

screens.name: DETERMINING_THE_PROBLEM_BY_SENDING_A_TEST_FAX
screens.label: DETERMINING THE PROBLEM BY SENDING A TEST FAX

fields.name: tile4a
fields.fieldText:
DETERMINING THE PROBLEM BY SENDING A TEST FAX Let the customer know that for you to further isolate the problem, a test fax would need to be sent. Ask the customer to resend the same fax that failed to the same number using Email-to-Fax and have the customer carbon copy (CC) your work email address. NOTE: If there are confidential documents in the original email, ask the customer to compose a new email instead then attach a non-confidential document to be sent as fax. WHY IS CARBON COPYING YOUR WORK EMAIL ADDRESS IMPORTANT Carbon copying your work email when sending test faxes will let you easily figure out what could be causing failures when sending faxes using email.
  • You will be able to determine the email addresses the customer is sending the email from.
    • Some customers are using email clients that support multiple email accounts. Using Email-to-Fax from the correct email address is critical in ensuring that faxes will be processed by the RingCentral processing server.
  • You will be able to determine if there are non-supported documents included in the email that may prevent faxes from being sent out.
  • You will be able to figure out why cover pages are still being included even if the customer specifically chooses not to send one.
  • You will be able to determine if the email service of the customer is working which may instantly answer why sending faxes using email is not working.

screens.name: Email_to_Fax_Troubleshooting
screens.label: Email-to-Fax Troubleshooting

fields.name: Tile1
fields.fieldText:
Email to Fax This guide will walk you through the proper identification and resolution of an Email-to-Fax issue. Each Email-to-Fax issue should be handled individually and all information you've gathered must be recorded in the case. NOTE: Email-to-Fax is a feature that lets RingCentral customers send faxes using their emails. Should you have issues receiving faxes through email, self-help can be accessed through our support site: Messages & Notifications - Customize User's Settings PREREQUISITES Before you start following this guide, please ensure that ALL of the following settings are correct:
  • User Extension status
    • Must be Enabled or Not Activated.
  • The email address where the faxes will be sent from should be added to the extension's Trusted Email Addresses list.
    • Self-help can be accessed through our support site: Fax - Configure Email allowed to send Faxes
    • Ensure that the email address is only added to 1 User Extension's Trusted Email Addresses list. If the email address is added to more than 1 User Extension's Trusted Email Addresses list, RingCentral will not be able to identify which extension is sending the fax, thus the fax will fail to send.
NOTE: The Email Address of the User Extension is automatically considered "trusted". Click "Next" to proceed Email-to-Fax Troubleshooting

NOTE: Please follow the proper verification process when removing email addresses from a different account. SEND ANOTHER TEST FAX TO TEST RESOLUTION Let the customer know that for you to further isolate the problem, another test fax would need to be sent. Ask the customer to resend the same fax that failed to the same number using Email-to-Fax and have the customer carbon copy (CC) your work email address. REFRESH THE FAX LOG RESULTS AND DETERMINE IF THE TEST FAX WILL SHOW UP Once the results are loaded, it will show up a list of all faxes that were processed by RingCentral in the account within the specific date range. The image above shows a 1-page fax request sent by albee.delacruz@ringcentral.com on 06/22/2017 at 5:58:31 PM. NOTE: An Email-to-Fax transaction processed by RingCentral will be indicated by a Message ID and Submit Date (date/time when RingCentral received the email) along with the trusted email address attempting to send a fax under the From Number. The results shown here does not automatically indicate that the fax was successfully sent by RingCentral. Click the Message ID to view the details of the fax transaction. The image above shows that the 1-page fax request sent by albee.delacruz@ringcentral.com was successfully sent to phone number: 1 (650) 539-3557 on 6/22/2017 at 5:59:42 PM.

  • Gather all important information in the Fax Log tool such as:
    • Message ID
    • Submit Date
    • Email address used
    • Recipient of the fax
  • Ensure that your case notes are detailed and concise.
  • Set expectations with the customer regarding their case being escalated.
  • Do not forget to select the correct Email-to-Fax disposition based on the issue being escalated.
  • Use probing questions to determine if the customer has any other unresolved issues. Take ownership and appropriate action to ensure unresolved issues are handled correctly.

ISSUE WITH THE RECEIVING FAX MACHINE If faxes sent using Email-to-Fax result to the status: Failed, this indicates that the Email-to-Fax process completed successfully and it is the actual sending of the fax to the number which failed. The factors that may affect the success rate of outbound faxes vary from: 1. Line quality issues 2. No answer from the receiving fax machine 3. The number is not a fax machine 4. The destination is an unallocated number 5. The number is constantly busy 6. The number is being answered by an voice answering service Self-help regarding these issues can be also accessed through our support site: https://success.ringcentral.com/articles/RC_Knowledge_Article/Fax-Troubleshooting-Checklist Issue is not with RingCentral. screens.label: ISSUE IDENTIFICATION

fields.name: Tile2
fields.fieldText:
ISSUE IDENTIFICATION Email-to-Fax issues vary depending on the symptoms customers are reporting. Below are the most common issues being reported and their corresponding symptoms: UNDESIRABLE BEHAVIORS WHEN SENDING FAXES USING EMAIL
  • General outbound fax failures Symptoms:
    • The fax transmission result show that the attempts to send the fax failed.
    • Fax was not received by the recipient though the fax transmission result indicated that it was successfuly sent.
    • Fax was not received by the recipient and no fax transmission result was generated to the sender.
  • Delays in sending faxes Symptoms:
    • The fax transmission result show that the fax was sent but it took a significant amount of time before the receipient has successfully received the fax.
    • The customer sent the email several minutes ago however they have not received the fax transmission result yet and the Call Log is not showing any information that the fax is being sent.
NOT RECEIVING FAX TRANSMISSION RESULTS Symptoms:
  • The recipient has successfuly received the fax however the tax transmission results are not being delivered to the notification email address.
  • Fax transmission results are being delivered to the wrong email address.
UNABLE TO REMOVE THE COVER PAGE WHEN SENDING FAXES USING EMAIL Symptoms:
  • Faxes sent using email always have a cover page even if the User Extension is set to not send a cover page.
  • A cover page is always being sent even if the customer is not puting any subject in the email being sent as faxes.

fields.name: tile5delays
fields.fieldText: ISSUE WITH THE RECEIVING FAX MACHINE If faxes sent using Email-to-Fax result to the status: Failed, this indicates that the Email-to-Fax process completed successfully and it is the actual sending of the fax to the number which failed. The factors that may affect the success rate of outbound faxes vary from: 1. Line quality issues 2. No answer from the receiving fax machine 3. The number is not a fax machine 4. The destination is an unallocated number 5. The number is constantly busy 6. The number is being answered by an voice answering service Self-help regarding these issues can be also accessed through our support site: https://success.ringcentral.com/articles/RC_Knowledge_Article/Fax-Troubleshooting-Checklist HOW TO DETERMINE IF THERE'S A DELAY WHEN SENDING THIS FAX Typically, an Email-to-Fax request can be processed by RingCentral within 2 minutes (from the time the Email-to-Fax request was received to the initial time the server attempts to send out the fax). However, this may vary depending on the work load of the RingCentral processing server at a given time. Ideally, it is best to give the RingCentral processing server at least 15 minutes to process the fax. If the outbound fax is taking more than 15 minutes to be processed, this should be reported to Tier 2. NOTE: The processing period indicated above does not include the actual duration of the fax transmission. The period being measured is only from the time the request was received to the time the server initially attempted to send the fax. The duration of the fax transmission will vary depending on the amount of data there is in the fax document. The results shown on the Fax Log tool will tell you when the request was received by RingCentral. This is indicated by the Submit Date. This marks the start of the processing period. NOTE: The image above indicates that the RingCentral processing server has received the Email-to-Fax request on 06/22/2017 at 7:27:55 PM. Zero (0) under the # of pages indicate that the RingCentral processing server has not yet determined the number of pages the actual fax will contain. Clicking the Message ID will provide you the details of the request and tell you the phone number of the receipient and the status of the request. Further clicking on the Recipient ID will provide you the actual time the RingCentral processing server initially attempted to send the fax. Simply calculate the difference of the Start Time of Retry # 0 and the data earlier under Submit Date. This marks the end of the processing period. NOTE: The image above indicates that the RingCentral processing server attempted to send the fax on 06/22/2017 at 7:31:09 PM. If the Email-to-Fax request was received on 06/22/2017 at 7:27:55 PM (Submit Date) and the initial sending started on 06/22/2017 at 8:59:20 PM (Start Time), the processing period is 1 hour, 31 minutes and 25 seconds.

fields.name: tile6fax
fields.fieldText:
NO FAX LOG RESULTS FOR THE REPORTED ISSUE If no fax log results are showing up, this indicates that the fax was not processed by RingCentral and will be considered a failure in sending faxes. The next steps will help you figure out why sending faxes via email are failing. DETERMINING THE PROBLEM BY SENDING A TEST FAX Let the customer know that for you to further isolate the problem, a test fax would need to be sent. Ask the customer to resend the same fax that failed to the same number using Email-to-Fax and have the customer carbon copy (CC) your work email address. NOTE: If there are confidential documents in the original email, ask the customer to compose a new email instead then attach a non-confidential document to be sent as fax. WHY IS CARBON COPYING YOUR WORK EMAIL ADDRESS IMPORTANT Carbon copying your work email when sending test faxes will let you easily figure out what could be causing failures when sending faxes using email.
  • You will be able to determine the email addresses the customer is sending the email from.
    • Some customers are using email clients that support multiple email accounts. Using Email-to-Fax from the correct email address is critical in ensuring that faxes will be processed by the RingCentral processing server.
  • You will be able to determine if there are non-supported documents included in the email that may prevent faxes from being sent out.
  • You will be able to figure out why cover pages are still being included even if the customer specifically chooses not to send one.
  • You will be able to determine if the email service of the customer is working which may instantly answer why sending faxes using email is not working.

fields.name: tile5d
fields.fieldText: ELABORATING THE STATUS: NOT RENDERED / MARKED The status Not rendered or Marked indicates that the RingCentral processing server has received the request to send the fax and is currently analyzing the document and/or cover page attached to the email. Though this is part of the normal routine in processing the sending of the fax, it may also indicate a problem with the RingCentral processing server specifically if it's taking a while for the status to change from Not rendered / Marked to Failed - Rendering Failed; Failed; or Sent. WHEN TO CONSIDER IF THE OUTBOUND FAX IS "TAKING A WHILE" TO BE SENT OUT If the outbound fax is taking a considerable time to be sent out, this may indicate a problem with the RingCentral processing server. Typically, an Email-to-Fax request can be processed by RingCentral within 2 minutes (from the time the Email-to-Fax request was received to the initial time the server attempts to send out the fax). However, this may vary depending on the work load of the RingCentral processing server at a given time. Ideally, it is best to give the RingCentral processing server at least 15 minutes to process the fax. If the outbound fax is taking more than 15 minutes to be processed, this should be reported to Tier 2. NOTE: The processing period indicated above does not include the actual duration of the fax transmission. The period being measured is only from the time the request was received to the time the server initially attempted to send the fax. The duration of the fax transmission will vary depending on the amount of data there is in the fax document. HOW TO IDENTIFY IF THE DURATION TO PROCESS THE FAX HAS ALREADY "TAKEN A WHILE" The results shown on the Fax Log tool will tell you when the request was received by RingCentral. This is indicated by the Submit Date. This marks the start time of the processing period NOTE: The image above indicates that the RingCentral processing server has received the Email-to-Fax request on 06/22/2017 at 7:27:55 PM. Zero (0) under the # of pages indicate that the RingCentral processing server has not yet determined the number of pages the actual fax will contain. Clicking the Message ID will provide you the details of the request. If no data is shown under Last Sending, simply calculate the difference of the current time and the data earlier under Submit Date.

fields.name: Tile3a

UNDESIRABLE BEHAVIORS WHEN SENDING FAXES USING EMAIL Below are the following issues pertaining to the behavior of sending faxes thru email:
  • General outbound fax failures Symptoms:
    • The fax transmission result show that the attempts to send the fax failed.
    • Fax was not received by the recipient though the fax transmission result indicated that it was successfuly sent.
    • Fax was not received by the recipient and no fax transmission result was generated to the sender.
  • Delays in sending faxes Symptoms:
    • The fax transmission result show that the fax was sent but it took a significant amount of time before the receipient has successfully received the fax.
    • The customer sent the email several minutes ago however they have not received the fax transmission result yet and the Call Log is not showing any information that the fax is being sent.
